##2) Biological trade-offs to memorize

### Sensitivity vs spatial resolution

- Sticks: high sensitivity, low resolution.
- Cones: better resolution and color, less efficient in low light.

### Temporal vs spatial resolution

- Channel M: fast, movement, less detailed.
- Channel P: more detailed, color, slower.

### Central vs peripheral vision

- Fovéa: maximum precision.
- Peripheral: wide field and movement detection.

---

##3) Modern interpretation of retinal coding

### Why center-surround?

- Objects are defined by local contrast, not absolute luminance.
- Difference coding reduces the necessary dynamics.

### Algorithmic consequence

- Oriented/derivative filters are naturally relevant in artificial vision.

---

##4) Focus cortex: from selectivity to invariance

- Simple cells: orientation + position.
- Complex cells: partial stability to translation.
- Hierarchy: increasing specificity + increasing robustness.

---

##5) Critical application: VR/AR and visual comfort

### Origin of the VAC conflict

- Real world: vergence and accommodation coupled.
- Stereo screen: vergence controlled by disparity, accommodation fixed on the screen.

### Common symptoms

- fatigue, discomfort, nausea, diplopia, decreased performance.

### Technological avenues

- light field near-eye;
- holographic displays;
- variable focal planes depending on the gaze.

---

##6) Flash Questions

- Why are M cells not optimal for color?
- Why is a low contrast image more difficult to perceive?
- How does retinotopy help cortical organization?
- Why can a VR system cause discomfort even with a clear image?

##7) Checklist before exam

- I master the rod/cone roles.
- I master M/P roles.
- I can describe retina -> LGN -> V1 -> dorsal/ventral.
- I can explain VAC in 3 precise sentences.
- I can relate a biological principle to a computer model.

---

##8) Common Mistakes

- Confusing binocular disparity and accommodation.
- Say that the entire retina has the same resolution.
- Assume purely feedforward processing in biology.
- Forget that perception and comfort do not only depend on sharpness.
